record.paper_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can an RIS channel model be derived that keeps the end-to-end channel in a factored form GΦH, while still capturing mutual impedances and coupling by allowing the RIS matrix Φ to become a possibly non-diagonal function of circuit parameters, and can a practical channel-estimation method be built for that model?

evidence.quote: A more interesting and useful model is one that retains the factored form GΦH, separating the statistical part of the Tx-RIS and RIS-Rx channels, but incorporating the effects of mutual impedances and coupling into the RIS matrix Φ, making it potentially non-diagonal and function of circuit model parameters. Obtaining such a factored model and the associated estimation technique is a potential direction for future research.

artifact.category_tag: RIS channel estimation with mutual coupling
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a wireless communication link assisted by a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) consisting of N reconfigurable scattering elements. Let H ∈ ℂ^{N×M} denote the channel from an M-antenna transmitter to the RIS elements, and let G ∈ ℂ^{K×N} denote the channel from the RIS elements to a K-antenna receiver. In the standard (idealized) model, the end-to-end channel from transmitter to receiver is written in the factored form

  H_e2e = G Φ H,

where Φ ∈ ℂ^{N×N} is a diagonal matrix whose n-th diagonal entry encodes the reflection coefficient applied by the n-th RIS element, and is parameterized by tunable circuit parameters (e.g. varactor capacitances or PIN-diode states). This idealization ignores electromagnetic mutual impedances and mutual coupling among the densely packed RIS elements.

Let S ∈ ℂ^{N×N} denote the (frequency-dependent, geometry-determined) mutual scattering/impedance matrix of the RIS array, and let Γ(c) ∈ ℂ^{N×N} be a diagonal matrix of element loads parameterized by the vector c ∈ ℝ^N (or ℂ^N) of tunable circuit parameters. A physically consistent multiport-network model leads to an RIS response matrix

  Φ(c) = f(S, Γ(c)),

which in general is non-diagonal and depends jointly on S and on the circuit parameters c.

The problem has two parts:

(1) Derivation. Determine whether there exists a channel model that (a) retains the strictly factored form H_e2e = G Φ(c) H, with G and H independent of c and depending only on the propagation environment between the transmitter / receiver and the RIS, and (b) faithfully captures the mutual-impedance and mutual-coupling effects of the RIS array through a (possibly non-diagonal) matrix Φ(c) that is an explicit function of the circuit parameters c and of the coupling/impedance data of the array.

(2) Estimation. Assuming such a factored model exists, design a practical pilot-based channel-estimation procedure that, from observed input–output measurements taken under a set of training configurations {c_t}, recovers the parameters of G and H (and, if needed, of the coupling structure) with computational and pilot overhead that scales favorably in N, K, and M.
artifact.status_search_result: Several works (2023–2025) develop physics-consistent multiport-network and scattering-parameter models for RIS in which the RIS response matrix becomes non-diagonal due to mutual coupling, and propose mutual-coupling-aware channel-estimation algorithms (e.g., compressed-sensing formulations, two-stage MC-unaware/MC-aware estimation, and BD-RIS modeling). These results provide candidate factored or near-factored representations and practical estimators, but a fully general factored model G Φ(c) H that exactly captures arbitrary mutual coupling while admitting a scalable estimator is still under active investigation, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Mutual Coupling-Aware Channel Estimation and Beamforming for RIS-Assisted Communications
status_evidence.snippet: Mutual coupling renders the RIS response non-diagonal; the paper develops a compressed-sensing formulation and a two-stage MC-unaware then MC-aware estimator.
status_evidence.claim: A practical mutual-coupling-aware RIS channel estimation method has been proposed.

status_evidence.title: On the Impact of Mutual Coupling on RIS-Assisted Channel Estimation
status_evidence.snippet: Under mutual coupling the RIS response is modeled as (Γ^{-1}-S)^{-1}, which is non-diagonal and invalidates standard estimators.
status_evidence.claim: A non-diagonal physics-consistent RIS matrix model has been derived; conventional estimators must be adapted.

status_evidence.title: Beyond Diagonal RIS with Mutual Coupling: Modeling and Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Derives a mutual-coupling-aware BD-RIS model using scattering/impedance parameters and addresses optimization.
status_evidence.claim: Non-diagonal RIS factored models incorporating mutual coupling have been formulated.

status_evidence.title: Ambiguity-Aware Segmented Estimation of Mutual Coupling in Large RIS
status_evidence.snippet: The number of mutual coupling parameters grows quadratically with N, motivating segmented estimation schemes.
status_evidence.claim: Scalable estimation of mutual coupling in large RIS is still an active research area.
